html:
The Armenian independence referendum was held on 21 September 1991, and more than 99 percent of voters chose to leave the Soviet Union. Independence was declared two days later.

The vote followed the Karabakh movement and the failed coup in Moscow. The new state faced war with Azerbaijan over Karabakh, a blockade by Azerbaijan and Turkey, and the ruin left by the 1988 earthquake. In the cold winters of the early 1990s Yerevan had power only an hour or two a day. Many people emigrated, swelling the diaspora. Armenia joined the United Nations in 1992 and kept close ties with Russia. The day is Independence Day in Armenia.
sum: The Armenian independence referendum was held on 21 September 1991, and more than 99 percent of voters chose to leave the Soviet Union. Independence was declared two days later.
